We have reported for the first time that serum creatinine and urinary Na (<5 mEq/l) at the time of diagnosis were associated with survival, suggesting that early treatment might increase survival in patients with hepatorenal syndrome. However, we also found that leptin levels did not provide prognostic indications in advanced lung cancer patients. Additionally, we did not find any association between serum leptin levels and prognosis in patients with well-differentiated small hepatocellular carcinoma or those undergoing staging laparoscopy for hepatocellular carcinoma.

These findings suggest that there may be additional prognostic factors that are not yet fully understood, and further research is needed to determine the significance of these variables. However, early treatment could potentially increase survival in patients with hepatorenal syndrome, highlighting the importance of considering this condition when evaluating the prognosis of these patients.
